strings.name: Max Verstappen
strings.role: Racing driver · Four-time F1 world champion
strings.summary: Born into a racing family in Belgium, Verstappen races for the Netherlands. He progressed through karting and European Formula 3, made his F1 debut at seventeen and won on his Red Bull debut at eighteen. Four consecutive drivers’ titles from 2021 to 2024 included nineteen wins in 2023. His speed and uncompromising racing brought Red Bull success and recurring debate about driving standards and rules.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: Represented the highest level of contemporary motor racing through consecutive Formula1 world titles and season records.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Racing family
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Father Jos raced in F1; mother Sophie competed in karting
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Four consecutive world titles
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won the F1 drivers’ championship in every season from 2021 to 2024.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Nineteen wins in one season
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Won nineteen Grands Prix in 2023, including a run of ten consecutive victories.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: From 21st to second in São Paulo
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Finished second after starting 21st because of engine penalties in a wet São Paulo Grand Prix.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Won the Mexico City Grand Prix
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Won ahead of Lewis Hamilton as Kimi Antonelli secured the season’s drivers’ title.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Fourth drivers’ championship
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Secured the title in Las Vegas for his fourth consecutive championship since 2021.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Nineteen wins and ten in a row
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Won nineteen Grands Prix, including ten consecutively, in his third title-winning season.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Second world championship
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Retained his title with fifteen wins in the first season under new technical regulations.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: First F1 world title
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Passed Hamilton on the final lap in Abu Dhabi for his first title amid controversy over the safety-car restart.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Won on his Red Bull debut
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won the Spanish Grand Prix after promotion from Toro Rosso, becoming F1’s youngest race winner at eighteen.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: F1 debut at seventeen
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Debuted for Toro Rosso at the Australian Grand Prix as the youngest F1 driver.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: European Formula 3 season
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Moved into single-seaters, finished third in European F3 and joined the Red Bull Junior Team.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: World karting champion
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Won the KZ world karting championship and European titles before moving into single-seaters.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born into a racing family
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Hasselt to parents with racing backgrounds and began karting in childhood under his father’s guidance.
